findings: PRIMARY MARKET/TREND ANGLE: Enterprise AI is converging on 'governance-first multi-agent orchestration.' Buyers are no longer paying for raw multi-agent capability; they pay for an orchestration control plane that enforces permissions, observability, audit trails, review gates, and human-in-the-loop authority. This project's code-enforced authority model (capability != permission != authority), least-privilege per-role tool sets, no-self-escalation rule, and BadSector adversarial review gate align directly with that demand — the harness is effectively an 'agent governance platform', not just another agent framework.

Framework phase and consolidation: 2024-2025 produced a wave of orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen -> Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Semantic Kernel, LlamaIndex Workflows, AWS Bedrock AgentCore) followed by rapid consolidation (AutoGen folded into Agent Framework; CrewAI-AutoGen merger announced 2025; LangChain unifying LangGraph/LangSmith/Langfuse). Strategic implication: betting on a single framework is a liability; protocol-level interoperability and an opinionated control plane are the durable differentiators.

Protocol standardization is the dominant interop trend: MCP (Model Context Protocol) became the de facto standard for tool/context connectivity (adopted by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic), and A2A (Agent2Agent) for inter-agent communication was donated to the Linux Foundation in mid-2025, signaling an emerging 'agent mesh / agentic internet' where agents from different vendors interoperate. A harness built on MCP/A2A-compatible boundaries is future-proof; a closed one risks obsolescence.

Quality problem is the market's pain point: research such as the MAST taxonomy ('Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?', 2025) documents 14 failure modes — error compounding across agents, context contamination, role confusion, evaluation difficulty — and evidence shows a well-tooled single agent can beat naive multi-agent setups. The market is therefore shifting from 'more agents' to 'more discipline': evals, tracing, guardrails, and deterministic authority boundaries. This project's design (peer relationships, no subdelegation, external output as untrusted data) is a direct answer to these failure modes.

Enterprise adoption and economics: analyst projections (Gartner) put agentic AI in ~33% of enterprise software by 2028 (from <1% in 2024), ~15% of day-to-day work decisions autonomous by 2028, and 40% of agentic AI projects canceled by 2027 due to scope creep, unclear ROI, and cost; market sizing (e.g., MarketsandMarkets) ranges roughly $5B (2024) to ~$47B (2030). Pricing is migrating from per-token to per-task/outcome models, and token cost plus latency budgets are first-class design constraints for orchestration layers.

Most commercially validated agent category is agentic coding/DevOps agents (e.g., Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, agentic CI/CD), where ROI is measurable — which is exactly this project's domain (a multi-agent development harness), making the trend directly relevant rather than adjacent.

Counter-trend to watch: 'agent fatigue' and skepticism (agents dismissed as fancy RAG), plus vendor consolidation churn. Positioning must lead with measurable outcomes, governance, and auditability rather than agent hype, which matches the project's conservative, authority-gated design.
evidence: Gartner predictions (2025): 33% of enterprise software will include agentic AI by 2028; 40% of agentic AI projects canceled by 2027; 15% of day-to-day work decisions autonomous by 2028.
Market sizing (MarketsandMarkets, directional): AI agents market from ~$5B (2024) to ~$47B (2030).
MCP adopted as cross-vendor standard by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic; A2A protocol donated to the Linux Foundation (June 2025).

Observability/eval stack consolidation (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, AgentOps, OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions) as evidence that governance/observability is the fastest-growing orchestration sub-market.

Strategic implication: betting on a single framework is a liability; protocol-level interoperability and an opinionated control plane are the durable differentiators.

Protocol standardization is the dominant interop trend: MCP (Model Context Protocol) became the de facto standard for tool/context connectivity (adopted by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic), and A2A (Agent2Agent) for inter-agent communication was donated to the Linux Foundation in mid-2025, signaling an emerging 'agent mesh / agentic internet' where agents from different vendors interoperate. A harness built on MCP/A2A-compatible boundaries is future-proof; a closed one risks obsolescence.

Quality problem is the market's pain point: research such as the MAST taxonomy ('Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?', 2025) documents 14 failure modes — error compounding across agents, context contamination, role confusion, evaluation difficulty — and evidence shows a well-tooled single agent can beat naive multi-agent setups. The market is therefore shifting from 'more agents' to 'more discipline': evals, tracing, guardrails, and deterministic authority boundaries. This project's design (peer relationships, no subdelegation, external output as untrusted data) is a direct answer to these failure modes.

Enterprise adoption and economics: analyst projections (Gartner) put agentic AI in ~33% of enterprise software by 2028 (from <1% in 2024), ~15% of day-to-day work decisions autonomous by 2028, and 40% of agentic AI projects canceled by 2027 due to scope creep, unclear ROI, and cost; market sizing (e.g., MarketsandMarkets) ranges roughly $5B (2024) to ~$47B (2030). Pricing is migrating from per-token to per-task/outcome models, and token cost plus latency budgets are first-class design constraints for orchestration layers.

Most commercially validated agent category is agentic coding/DevOps agents (e.g., Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, agentic CI/CD), where ROI is measurable — which is exactly this project's domain (a multi-agent development harness), making the trend directly relevant rather than adjacent.

Counter-trend to watch: 'agent fatigue' and skepticism (agents dismissed as fancy RAG), plus vendor consolidation churn. Positioning must lead with measurable outcomes, governance, and auditability rather than agent hype, which matches the project's conservative, authority-gated design.
